sam: Heads up — seeing a 95p tail latency spike on canary for continuous-batcher starting ~15:20 UTC, coincides with kernel-selector flip.
anya: saw it too, dashboard shows microbatch size collapse from ~32 to ~6 on affected hosts.
mike: hmm that suggests admission started favoring low-latency path and broke batching. Any noisy tenant?
kevin: host-level metrics show one tenant with bursty small requests at that time, but kernel change also changed kv-cache shard mapping. possible interaction.
sam: attaching profiler snippet:
```
perf: top kernels by time
fused_attention_v2  42%  (was 18% before flip)
matmul_opt_1       28%
kv_cache_serialize 15%
other              15%
```
anya: fused_attention_v2 is much heavier for short sequences — it increases per-request overhead if batching is tiny.
mike: admission control logs: `admission: microbatch_target=32 -> 8 (policy=latency_prefer)` at 15:19:50
kevin: and kernel-selector log: `kernel_select: chosen=fused_attention_v2 for model=llama-13b, seq=64, heuristic_score=0.82` at same time.
sam: so timeline is: kernel selector flips -> more expensive kernel for small batches -> admission shrinks microbatch -> less batching -> higher overhead -> tail spikes. plus kv-cache shard remap caused by kernel change?
anya: kv-cache metric shows eviction_rate spiked 3x right after — probably because fused_attention path serializes kv hits differently.
mike: can we repro locally? I can run a stress with a noisy tenant mix + kernel flag flip. will try in perf-staging.
kevin: mitigation: roll back kernel selector to prior heuristics (pin kernel variant) and nudge admission to prefer batch size floor=16.
sam: agree. also add temporary rule to route noisy tenant to dedicated pool to reduce noise while we root cause.
sre-oncall: scheduling remediation: rollback scheduled, rollback window 15min, will monitor.
perf-bot: run perf-regression-check job queued (job-id=PRC-4721).
anya: action items: 1) mike -> repro and attach flamegraphs (due in 4h). 2) kevin -> add pinning toggle and batch-floor config (due 2h). 3) sam -> tenant diversion playbook (due 1h). 4) infra -> monitor KV eviction metric and tail 95/99.
mike: repro started in perf-staging, seeing same microbatch collapse when kernel flag toggled. sharing flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/staging/PRC-4721/flamegraph
kevin: quick patch to admission: `min_microbatch_size=16` pushed to canary, watch for regressions.
sam: thanks. if rollback restores tail -> good candidate for fallback policy: if tail_95 > baseline*1.5 and batch_size < 12 then prefer previous kernel.
anya: adding that rule to the scheduler playbook now.
sre-oncall: monitoring shows tail latency trending down after rollback started. will keep open for 1hr.
mike: one note — fused_attention_v2 improves throughput for long sequences; need a more nuanced selector that considers batch estimate and kv-serialize cost.
eke: agree — long-term: include kv-serialize cost and dynamic tenant signal into kernel scoring.
sam: OK let's follow up in eng-runtime tomorrow with profiling artifacts and a proposal for kernel-scoring delta. closing this thread once metrics stable. :thumbsup:
